payload.evidence: BOTH HALVES, and the row required both. RULES LIBRARY (dc, 07d49a2e): `IN-AG-FIAT-001` ships in the agnostic pack, severity critical, validator 9 ok and `rule_pack_agnostic` 11 ok. It is one of the two PROCEDURAL agnostic rules with `red-control`, so it carries no `concretised_by`, and the schema and `intent/docs/rules.md` were amended in the same commit to say why -- the anti-vagueness obligation does not lapse, it changes form, and a procedural rule discharges it through `applies_when` naming SITUATIONS rather than virtues. SKILLS (ic, 009299a4): `in-essentials` section 8 names the id and points at `intent claude rules show IN-AG-FIAT-001` rather than restating it, because a second copy of a rule's content in a skill is the Highlander violation the library exists to prevent. THE DETECTION SECTION STATES WHAT IS AND IS NOT MECHANICALLY CHECKABLE, which is the clause the row spends its second half on: checkable is `fc` in committed automation (the one arm a critic can enforce outright, since automation has no human at a keyboard by definition), a record whose invoker evidence says no tty, a `because` restating the criterion, and a close landing in the session it unblocks; NOT checkable is whether a human or an LLM typed it (same uid, same shell, no field settles it and none can be added on this machine), tty-or-not (an agent can allocate one and a human's own `fc` in a script or ssh pipe has none), and whether the human's ruling actually happened. Enforcement is DETECTION PLUS ATTRIBUTION, NEVER A CLAIMED IMPOSSIBILITY -- stated as such because a false claim in a contract invites the reader to conclude that because nothing stopped them, nothing forbade them, and both the rule and ic's skill bullet say so in as many words. `ships in the relevant skills` is read as the CANON skill, which is the artefact that ships; the per-machine installed copy under ~/.claude is a local install product and propagating it machine-wide was correctly left for hv.
